Architecture

Why multiple agents instead of one big prompt?

Focused Prompts
Each agent has one job, its own system prompt, and a Pydantic output schema. No cross-stage contamination
Isolated Tools
Sub-agents only get the tools they need. PricingAgent can't call finalize_loan_decision. No tool leakage
Testable Boundaries
Each agent writes structured output to a session state key. Test underwriting in isolation, swap pricing logic independently
Locked Down
Sub-agents set disallow_transfer_to_parent and disallow_transfer_to_peers to True. They can't call other agents

Architecture

The four-agent pipeline

AutoRAG

AutoRAG — retrieval-augmented regulatory knowledge

How It Works
  • OGX vector store — Milvus + nomic-embed-text-v1.5 embeddings
  • UnderwritingAgent: 1 LLM tool call → internally 2 AutoRAG queries (eligibility rules + industry guidance)
  • LoanDecisionAgent: internal auto-call on decline path (ECOA adverse action via retrieve_regulatory_guidance)
  • max_num_results=3 per query — focused, low-latency retrieval
  • Graceful degradation: falls back to static eligibility_rules.json if AutoRAG unavailable
The 9-Document Corpus
  • SBA general eligibility + DSCR requirements
  • Collateral requirements + LTV table
  • Prohibited business types (13 CFR § 120.110)
  • Adverse action notice rules (ECOA / Reg B)
  • Prohibited NAICS codes (30 codes)
  • Industry risk assessment guide
  • Risk tier + rate pricing guide
  • Applicant FAQ (20 Q&A) + reapplication guidance

Safety

Callbacks — guardrails at every lifecycle point

HookCallbackWhat It Does
before_agentextract_request_idParses loan ID (SBL-YYYY-XXXXX) from user message; stores inline documents for later injection
before_toolhalt / skip guardBlocks execution if process is halted, completed, or pricing should be skipped (INELIGIBLE)
before_modelinject_documentInjects PDF/image into LLM request context — DocumentExtractionAgent only
after_agentstate_loggingPersists sub-agent output to SQLite; detects INELIGIBLE → flags PricingAgent skip
after_agentllm_judge_gateSecond LLM call validates trajectory, grounding, completeness. Fail → response blocked

LLM-as-Judge: checks tool order, verifies all numbers match structured outputs, confirms nothing missing. Fails closed — blocked response, not hallucinated data.

Resilience

Repair and resume — surviving failures and restarts

Three-Layer State
  • Layer 1: ADK session state — in-memory, fast, lost on pod restart
  • Layer 2: SQLite via ProcessStateService — persistent on PVC, full model_dump() of every agent output
  • Layer 3: check_process_status — always first tool call, bridges SQLite → ADK session on resume
  • Layer 4: _load_step_data_from_db() — last-resort fallback inside finalize_loan_decision for cross-turn sessions
Recovery Scenarios
  • Pod restart between pricing and approval → SQLite reloads completed steps into fresh session
  • Missing data mid-pipeline → agent halts, asks user, resumes from exact step
  • User returns hours later in new session → check_process_status picks up where it left off
  • Approval in fresh API session → _load_step_data_from_db() loads all prior outputs from SQLite

Platform

RHOAI capabilities used by this agent

Model Serving (MaaS)
Gemini 2.5 Flash via OpenAI-compatible endpoint through LiteLLM. Switch to Vertex AI or direct API key by changing env vars
AutoRAG (OGX)
9-doc regulatory corpus in Milvus + nomic-embed-text-v1.5. Queried 3× per loan: 2 at underwriting, 1 at loan decision
MLflow Tracing
Optional — set MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI and every LiteLLM call auto-logs as spans. Degrades gracefully if unavailable
OpenShift AI Deployment
FastAPI container, PVC for SQLite, ConfigMap for tunable params, SealedSecrets for API key, OpenShell network isolation

In Practice

What a real conversation looks like

  • User: "Process loan SBL-2026-10001: Acme Bakery, $150K, 5 years, $420K revenue..."
  • Pipeline: check_process_status → load_skill → DocumentExtractionAgent → UnderwritingAgent + 2 RAG queries → PricingAgent
  • Agent: "Acme Bakery qualifies as Tier 2 (Moderate Risk). 7.75% rate, $3,012.43/mo, 60 months. Do you approve?"
  • User: "Yes, approve it."
  • Pipeline: check_process_status (reload from SQLite) → LoanDecisionAgent → LLM-as-Judge → response
  • Agent: "Loan SBL-2026-10001 approved. Approval letter generated (ref: DL-2026-10001)."
